meta.seoTitle: Your first developer job: a guide
meta.title: How to land your first developer job in 2026
meta.description: Resume, LinkedIn, portfolio, projects, networking and interviews: practical advice for landing your first developer job.
meta.excerpt: A practical approach to building credibility, finding opportunities and preparing for interviews as a junior developer.
meta.coverAlt: Person working on a laptop near a window.

content.text: Finding your first job in development is not just about technical skills. You also need to demonstrate them, build trust and create more opportunities to meet the right people.
I have brought together the advice I regularly share with junior developers, with a practical approach to taking action.

sections.title: Build the three pillars of your credibility

content.text: Before sending out more applications, get three things up to date: your resume, your LinkedIn profile and your portfolio.
A recruiter should be able to identify the role you are targeting and find concrete examples of what you can do.

blocks.text: A readable resume tailored to the role

items.text: Layout:
Choose a clean, spacious template with a readable text structure. Avoid overly complex or purely graphical designs.
Clarity:
Write short descriptions focused on your responsibilities and achievements. Leave out details unrelated to the role.
Evidence:
Give concrete examples of your achievements.
Proofreading:
Have someone review your resume and ask an AI tool to flag ambiguous wording. Check each suggestion before keeping it.
Format:
Prepare a clean, lightweight PDF with a structure that applicant tracking systems (ATS) can read.

content.text: For applications in France, consider a well-presented photo essential. Choose a professional portrait with a well-lit face, a slight smile, clear framing and a simple background. It helps shape the recruiter's first impression and identify you among applicants: take the time to present yourself well.
Place your target role and main technologies near the top of the page.

blocks.text: A LinkedIn profile that explains your positioning

items.text: Clear headline:
State the role you are looking for and the technologies you use.
Completeness:
Detail your relevant experience and projects, and add your technical skills. Include links to your GitHub and portfolio.
Clarity:
Explain the value you bring. Avoid vague wording and lists of buzzwords.
Social proof:
Ask former colleagues or instructors for recommendations.

content.text: Example of an effective headline
Junior Fullstack Developer | React • TypeScript • Node.js | Seeking a permanent role
Use the same job title and key skills on your resume and LinkedIn.

blocks.text: A portfolio that demonstrates your skills

items.text: Selection:
Present your specialization and select your most relevant projects. Show real, working applications.
Context:
For each project, explain the problem you solved, the technologies you used and the reasons behind your technical choices.
Access:
Make live demos and GitHub repositories easy to access.
Technical quality:
Test the mobile layout, keyboard accessibility and performance. Check links and fix any errors you find.

content.text: For a team project, clearly distinguish your contribution from the team's work.
These materials do not guarantee a job. They give recruiters concrete examples to assess your profile and the projects you can present.
Job listings are not the only way in. By talking to people in the industry, you can ask for advice and sometimes learn that a team is preparing to hire.
Do not limit yourself to recruiters. Try to connect with people who understand your work and have relevant needs:
CTOs Tech Leads Engineering Managers Lead Developers Founders Product Managers
Send a few targeted invitations and personalize each message.

Write a short message explaining your background and what interests you about the company. For an initial conversation, you can also ask for advice or offer help, rather than opening with a request for a job.

blocks.title: Outreach message template
blocks.code:
Hello [First name],

I came across your work at [Company] and am particularly interested in [specific aspect of the product or engineering team].

I am a junior developer specializing in [technologies] and am currently looking for [type of opportunity].

Do you have any advice on how I could get closer to a team like yours?

Thank you for your time.

content.text: ⚠️ This template must be personalized for the context. It is not a message to send in bulk.
Job searching takes consistency. Combine responses to job listings, speculative applications and direct outreach.

items.text: Check several platforms, not just LinkedIn. Visit companies' careers pages.
Identify companies that use your technology stack.
Do not wait until you meet 100% of a listing's criteria before applying.
Tailor your applications to the companies that genuinely interest you.

content.text: Do not focus only on tech giants.
Small and medium-sized businesses, web agencies, specialist software vendors, regional companies and less visible startups offer excellent opportunities to get started.

sections.title: Create content to become more visible

content.text: Creating content lets you show your progress, share your knowledge and become more than an anonymous profile. The goal is not to become an influencer, but to document your work.
Lessons from experience
"I ran into this performance issue. Here is how I solved it."
Learning
"Here are three things I understood while learning TypeScript this week."
Demo
"A short video showing how my new application works."
Comparison
"REST or GraphQL: here are the practical differences I have observed."

items.text: Consistency:
Set a sustainable pace. Do not sacrifice your technical learning to create content.
Authenticity:
Write in your own words. AI can help with corrections, but the experience should be yours.
Interaction:
Leave relevant comments on professionals' posts and regularly take part in technical discussions.

content.text: Prepare for interviews around four common situations:
Be ready to introduce your background and motivation in a few sentences. If you are changing careers, explain what led you to development. Prepare questions about the company.

blocks.title: AI practice prompt
blocks.code: Act as a demanding technical recruiter interviewing a junior developer. Ask me questions one at a time. Wait for my answer before continuing. After each answer, assess its clarity and relevance, and identify what is missing.

content.text: Practice on
CodinGame
or LeetCode. Break down the problem before coding and explain your reasoning out loud. Your approach matters as much as the result.
Master the fundamentals of your stack. Understand the concepts rather than reciting definitions. Be able to say, "I do not know, but here is how I would investigate."
You may be asked to design the architecture of a simple app. Identify the business need, choose the database, front end and API, and explain your technical trade-offs.
Keep a tracking table in Notion or Excel to record applications sent, planned follow-ups and responses received.
Technical meetups, recruitment events and local conferences give you opportunities to talk directly with professionals. After meeting someone, connect on LinkedIn and mention what you discussed.

sections.title: Ten more tips to stand out

description.text: It is better to be known for a specific stack than to describe yourself as an expert in everything.

content.text: Action: Define your target role and stack in one sentence.

description.text: The basics of JavaScript, HTML/CSS, HTTP and SQL will serve you across projects, even as frameworks change.

content.text: Action: Review asynchronous programming, DOM manipulation and APIs.

description.text: It provides concrete evidence of how you code and document your work.

content.text: Action: Pin a few representative projects with explanatory READMEs.

description.text: , with design, architecture, stack choices, mockups and tests, says more than a list of unfinished tutorials.

content.text: Action: Choose a manageable scope and document your technical choices and error handling.

items.title: #5 Show how you work in a team

description.text: An open-source contribution or a hackathon can give you a concrete experience to discuss in an interview.

content.text: Action: Describe your role, the decisions made as a team and how the work was shared.

description.text: A targeted application lets you connect your profile to the role's requirements.

content.text: Action: Link a requested skill to an example from your projects.

description.text: Former classmates or instructors can tell you about companies that are hiring.

content.text: Action: Ask for targeted introductions.

description.text: Explaining a problem and asking for help are also part of teamwork.

content.text: Action: Explain what you tried, the result and the help you need.

description.text: An assistant to help you move faster, not a crutch that writes code for you.

content.text: Action: Understand and test every line suggested by AI.

description.text: After several applications without a response, check whether the roles you are targeting match your profile.

content.text: Action: Compare the listings with your resume and projects, then adjust your targets or how you present them.

items.text: Applying with a rushed or unfinished resume. Before your first application, finish a polished resume: clear, free of mistakes, well presented and tailored to the role. This preparation is the foundation for being competitive and avoiding wasting your first opportunities.
Confusing a high volume of indiscriminate applications with effectiveness.
Confusing LinkedIn popularity with real development skills.
Claiming to master technologies you do not really understand in depth.
Presenting a project generated entirely by AI without being able to explain its architecture.

content.text: Start by updating your resume and choosing a few projects you can present. Target companies hiring for your stack, track your applications and adjust them based on the conversations you have.
